quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: Intersections ahead.
Road construction.
A curve in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to what is coming up. This sign warns you about an upcoming right curve.

questions.question: When you see a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.
Wait four seconds before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. Turn in the direction the arrow points. First, yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: When must you use your low beams?

options.text: On a lit street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off these conditions and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights you can use with low beams.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, you should:

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Motorcycle operators have the right to:

options.text: Use a complete traffic lane.
Use half of a traffic lane.
Use the shoulder of a roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a complete traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists have the right to use a complete traffic lane. Two motorcyclists may share a lane if they want to. Do not pass a motorcycle within the same lane.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your freeway lane. You should:

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
Speed up to keep your position.
Always stay in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
questions.explanation: When you can, make room for vehicles to merge into your lane safely.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Use only your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Do not rely on mirrors alone because they do not show what is directly behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Check the inside rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: Strong wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Only affect large vehicles.
Only cause visibility problems.
Can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind can blow dirt and dust onto the road, reducing visibility. It can also physically push vehicles.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a gap large enough to safely enter the flow of traffic. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there are no safe gaps to merge into.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield the right-of-way.
No passing zone.
Reduction in lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular sign means you must yield the right-of-way to other vehicles.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is the top cause of traffic crashes. Any distraction can make you miss important sights and sounds that help you avoid accidents.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Keep checking your mirrors and blind spots.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep checking your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can hide in your blind spot or be missed because they are small. You must always look carefully for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters on the road.

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you has its red lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and go when you think all children have left the bus.
Slow to 25 mph and pass with care.
Stop and wait until the red lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the red lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. The only exception is if the bus is on the other side of a divided highway.

questions.question: Why should you use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, other drivers cannot see you easily. Your headlights make your vehicle more visible. If you need to use your windshield wipers, you must also use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: What is the amount of alcohol in your blood called?

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC number means more impairment.

questions.question: Oncoming headlights are blinding you at night. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights blind you, look at the right edge of the road instead of straight ahead. This keeps your vehicle on the road safely until you pass the other car.

questions.question: When is it most important to be careful when turning or stopping in rain?

options.text: After it has rained all day.
One half hour after the rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when turning and stopping during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars has not yet washed off the pavement and mixes with rain to create a slippery surface.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, how fast should you be driving?

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
Slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going over the speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction or maintenance area.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road construction or maintenance area.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards. Orange color is used for warning signs in construction or maintenance areas.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: You can eliminate them by having one outside mirror on each side of your vehicle.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger cars.
You can check blind spots by looking in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots. Other drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Cars passing you.
Cars coming toward you.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars coming toward you.
questions.explanation: You must yield to oncoming traffic when turning left. You can only turn when it is safe and you will not interfere with oncoming cars.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, it is hard to see and be seen. The best way to show other drivers you are there is to turn on:

options.text: Your dashboard lights.
Your parking lights.
Your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when other drivers cannot see you. Use your low beam headlights if you need to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your ability to drive safely?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your driving ability.

questions.question: To help avoid skidding on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after you start down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while in a curve can cause you to skid.
